title: Chapter 126 — Phone Etiquette
intro: The phone is still the front door for most service interactions.

sections.title: The 3-Ring Rule
sections.content:
Answer within 3 rings. Every ring beyond three tells the customer they are not a priority. If you cannot answer, let it go to a professional voicemail and return the call within one hour.

When answering: 'Thank you for calling [store], this is [name]. How can I help you?' Stand up when you take the call — your voice sounds better standing. Smile — they can hear it.

sections.title: Hold Procedures
sections.content:
Always ask permission before placing someone on hold. 'Do you mind if I put you on a brief hold while I check on that?' Check back every 60 seconds so the customer never feels forgotten. 'I am still looking into this — I should have an answer in about one more minute.'

If the hold will be more than 2 minutes, offer a callback. 'This is going to take a few minutes to track down. Can I call you back in about 10 minutes with the answer?' Then call back in 8 minutes. Early beats late.

sections.title: Warm vs Cold Transfers
sections.content:
A warm transfer means you introduce the customer to the next person before hanging up. 'Let me connect you with Sarah in service — she handles warranty claims. Sarah, I have [customer name] on the line — they need help with a warranty claim on their Bosch dishwasher purchased in March.'

A cold transfer means you dump them into voicemail or another extension with no context. Cold transfers tell the customer 'you are not worth my time.' Never cold transfer.
